learn.hook: Nani wants to sew a lace border all around her quilt. How much lace does she need? That length is the perimeter!
points: Perimeter is the total length of the boundary (the edge all around) of a shape.
To find it, add the lengths of all the sides.
Rectangle: perimeter = length + breadth + length + breadth = 2 × (length + breadth).
Square: all 4 sides are equal, so perimeter = 4 × side.
Perimeter is measured in units of length: cm, m or km.

example.q: Nani's quilt is a rectangle 3 m long and 2 m wide. How much lace goes around it?

learn.reallife: Fences around a field, frames around a photo and the boundary of a cricket ground are perimeters.

games.title: True or false?
items: Perimeter is the distance all around a shape.
It is the length of the boundary.
The perimeter of a square is 4 × side.
A rectangle 5 cm by 2 cm has a perimeter of 10 cm.
5 + 2 + 5 + 2 = 14 cm. 10 is the area in square cm.
Perimeter can be measured in cm, m or km.
Perimeter is measured in square units.
Square units are for area. Perimeter is a length.

quiz.q: What is the perimeter of a rectangle 8 cm long and 5 cm wide?
quiz.mistake: Adds only two sides (13 cm) or multiplies (40)

quiz.q: What is the perimeter of a square with side 7 cm?
quiz.explain: A square has 4 equal sides: 4 × 7 = 28 cm.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies 7 × 7, which gives the area

quiz.q: A triangle has sides 5 cm, 6 cm and 7 cm. What is its perimeter?
quiz.mistake: Adds only two sides, or multiplies

quiz.q: Nani's square table cloth has sides of 2 m. How much lace goes all around it?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies 2 × 2, which is the area

quiz.q: A garden is 20 m long and 15 m wide. How long is the fence around it?
quiz.mistake: Adds only one length and one breadth

quiz.q: The perimeter of a square is 36 cm. How long is each side?
quiz.explain: A square has 4 equal sides: 36 ÷ 4 = 9 cm.
quiz.mistake: Divides by 2 instead of 4

quiz.q: A rectangle has a perimeter of 30 cm. Its length is 10 cm. What is its breadth?
quiz.explain: Length + breadth is half the perimeter: 30 ÷ 2 = 15. Breadth = 15 − 10 = 5 cm.
quiz.mistake: Takes 10 away from 30 without halving first

quiz.q: Which has the longer perimeter: a square with side 6 cm, or a rectangle 8 cm by 3 cm?
quiz.mistake: Thinks the shape with the longest side has the bigger perimeter

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'What is perimeter? How do I find it for my nest?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Perimeter is the length all around. Just add all the sides!
teach.nudge: Is perimeter inside or around a shape? What do I do with the sides?

learn.hook: Nani's quilt is made of little square patches. Count the patches and you know how much the quilt covers!
points: Area is the amount of surface a shape covers.
We measure area by counting unit squares. A 1 cm by 1 cm square has an area of 1 square cm (1 sq cm).
For a rectangle, area = length × breadth. 5 rows of 3 squares = 15 square units.
Two half squares make one full square.
Area uses square units: sq cm, sq m.

example.q: Nani's quilt has 6 patches along its length and 4 along its width. Each patch is 1 square unit. What is its area?

learn.reallife: Painters, carpet sellers and farmers all think about area.

games.title: Area or perimeter?
items: Border tape around a notice board

quiz.q: What is the area of a rectangle 5 cm long and 3 cm wide?
quiz.mistake: Finds the perimeter (16 cm) instead of the area

quiz.q: What is the area of a square with side 6 cm?
quiz.mistake: Finds the perimeter (4 × 6 = 24) instead

quiz.q: A shape covers 8 full squares and 4 half squares. What is its area?
quiz.explain: 4 half squares make 2 full squares. 8 + 2 = 10 square units.
quiz.mistake: Counts each half square as a full square

quiz.q: Nani's quilt has 7 rows of 5 patches. How many patches are there?
quiz.mistake: Adds rows and patches instead of multiplying

quiz.q: Which unit should we use for the area of a notebook cover?
quiz.explain: Area is measured in square units. A notebook is small, so square centimetres fit.
quiz.mistake: Uses a unit of length for area

quiz.q: A room floor is 4 m by 3 m. Each tile covers 1 sq m. How many tiles cover the floor?
quiz.mistake: Adds length and breadth, or finds the perimeter

quiz.q: A rectangle has an area of 24 sq cm. Its length is 6 cm. What is its breadth?
quiz.explain: Length × breadth = area, so breadth = 24 ÷ 6 = 4 cm.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts 6 from 24

quiz.q: Arjun says the area of a square with side 3 cm is 12 sq cm. What went wrong?
options: He found the perimeter, not the area
quiz.explain: 4 × 3 = 12 is the perimeter. The area is 3 × 3 = 9 sq cm.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up area and perimeter

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'What is area? How is it different from the border?'
teach.praise: Wow! Area is how much space a shape covers, counted in squares!
teach.nudge: Is area the edge or the inside? How do we count it?

learn.hook: Nani has 12 square patches. She can make a long thin quilt or a fat one. Same area, but will the border be the same?
points: Shapes with the same area can have different perimeters.
Shapes with the same perimeter can have different areas.
For 12 squares: 3 by 4 has perimeter 14, 2 by 6 has 16, 1 by 12 has 26.
Remember the units: perimeter in cm or m, area in sq cm or sq m.

example.q: Nani makes rectangles from 12 square patches (each side 1 unit). Find the perimeter of each.

learn.reallife: A farmer with a fixed length of fence can make fields of different sizes.

games.title: Same area, different borders
games.prompt: These rectangles each use 12 squares. Order them from smallest perimeter to largest

items.text: A 2 by 5 rectangle has an area of ___ sq units
A 2 by 5 rectangle has a perimeter of ___ units
A square with side 4 has an area of ___ sq units
Perimeter is measured in cm, but area is measured in ___

quiz.q: A 2 by 6 rectangle and a 3 by 4 rectangle are made of unit squares. What is the same about them?
quiz.explain: Both cover 12 squares (2 × 6 = 12, 3 × 4 = 12). Perimeters are 16 and 14.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the same area always means the same perimeter

quiz.q: What is the perimeter of a 1 by 12 rectangle?
quiz.mistake: Adds only one length and one breadth (13)

quiz.q: A 4 by 4 square and a 2 by 6 rectangle both have perimeter 16. Which has the bigger area?
quiz.explain: Square: 4 × 4 = 16 sq units. Rectangle: 2 × 6 = 12 sq units.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the same perimeter means the same area

quiz.q: Nani has 36 square patches. Which quilt shape uses all of them exactly?
quiz.mistake: Does not multiply to check

quiz.q: A rectangle has an area of 20 sq cm and a length of 5 cm. What is its perimeter?
quiz.mistake: Gives the area as the perimeter, or adds only two sides

quiz.q: A square has a perimeter of 20 cm. What is its area?
quiz.mistake: Thinks area equals perimeter

quiz.q: A room is 5 m by 4 m. Carpet costs ₹100 for each square metre. How much does the carpet cost?
quiz.mistake: Uses the perimeter (18 m) instead of the area

quiz.q: Kabir doubles both sides of a 3 cm by 2 cm rectangle to make 6 cm by 4 cm. What happens to the area?
quiz.explain: Old area: 3 × 2 = 6. New area: 6 × 4 = 24. 24 is 4 times 6.
quiz.mistake: Thinks doubling the sides doubles the area

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'If two quilts cover the same area, do they need the same border?'
teach.praise: Oh! Same area can have a different border. Long thin quilts need more lace!
teach.nudge: Can the border change even if the area stays the same? Which shape needs more lace?
